quests.hint: Link 'been meaning', 'ask whether', 'able to', 'take a look at it'.
quests.explanation: Every link in this sentence takes a consonant to a vowel, so it is easy to break in the wrong place. Keeping the line smooth makes an indirect request sound relaxed.
quests.textToSpeak: I've been meaning to ask whether you'd be able to take a look at it.
quests.instruction: Copy the linking and pacing exactly.

quests.hint: Link 'sit down with them' and 'go over the'.
quests.explanation: 'Sit down with them' and 'go over the' are phrasal verbs, so they naturally link. 'Them' is weak, which lets REAL-ly, SIT and DE-tails carry the plan.
quests.textToSpeak: What I'd really like to do is sit down with them and go over the details.
quests.instruction: Repeat with the same smooth, connected delivery.

quests.hint: Reduce 'it'd', 'we could', link 'get everyone on'.
quests.explanation: 'It'd' and 'could' are both compressed, so the sentence reaches GREAT and SAME PAGE quickly. Linking 'get everyone on' avoids a stumble in the middle.
quests.textToSpeak: It'd be great if we could get everyone on the same page before the launch.
quests.instruction: Match the speaker's connections between words.

quests.hint: Beats on MAN-aged, CUT, RE-sponse, FOR-ty, HUGE, IM-prove-ment.
quests.explanation: A long sentence with a percentage is easy to rush or slow down too much. Steady beats on the key words keep the numbers clear.
quests.textToSpeak: We've managed to cut the response time by nearly forty percent, which is a huge improvement.
quests.instruction: Listen for the rhythm, then repeat with the same timing.

quests.hint: Beats on THING, HOLD-ing, BACK, LACK, OWN-er-ship.
quests.explanation: The main clause sets a beat pattern that carries the sentence, with 'that's really' and 'us back is the' compressed.
quests.textToSpeak: The thing that's really holding us back is the lack of clear ownership.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and match the beat.

quests.hint: Beats on POINT, RUSH-ing, CON-fi-dent, WORK.
quests.explanation: 'There's no point' and 'if we're not' are both quick frames. The beats on POINT, RUSH-ing and CON-fi-dent carry the argument without making the sentence sound heavy.
quests.textToSpeak: There's no point rushing it if we're not confident it'll work.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the rhythm of the phrase.

quests.hint: Beats on com-MIT-tee, com-pre-HEN-sive, a-NAL-y-sis and RISKS.
quests.explanation: Formal words have long unstressed stretches, so reduction is essential. If every syllable of 'comprehensive' were equally loud, the sentence would sound robotic.
quests.textToSpeak: The committee has requested a comprehensive analysis of the potential risks.
quests.instruction: Listen for the weak syllables, then repeat them lightly.

quests.hint: Weak: 'need to', 'the', '-mental', 'of the'; beats on en-vi-ron-MEN-tal, IM-pact, de-VEL-op-ment.
quests.explanation: Long words have one strong syllable each: en-vi-ron-MEN-tal, IM-pact, de-VEL-op-ment. The other syllables stay short.
quests.textToSpeak: We need to consider the environmental impact of the proposed development.
quests.instruction: Copy the reduced vowels exactly as you hear them.

quests.hint: Weak: 'to the', 'has', 'for the'; beats on ac-CORD-ing, UN-em-PLOY-ment, con-SEC-u-tive.
quests.explanation: News-style sentences pack many syllables into a short time. Reducing the small words lets the stressed syllables of 'unemployment' and 'consecutive' carry the meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: According to the latest figures, unemployment has fallen for the third consecutive quarter.
quests.instruction: Match the speaker's weak forms as you repeat.

quests.hint: Blend 'did you' as 'di-ja'; link 'sent over'.
quests.explanation: The /d/ of 'did' and the /j/ of 'you' blend into /dʒ/, and 'sent over' links across a consonant. Together they make an everyday question sound natural, not scripted.
quests.textToSpeak: Where did you save the version I sent over?
quests.instruction: Copy the linking and pacing exactly.

quests.hint: Blend 'would you', link 'mind if I asked you' and 'couple of'.
quests.explanation: The polite opening 'would you mind if I' contains four weak words in a row. Blending and linking them keeps the request light so the actual topic, QUES-tions, is heard.
quests.textToSpeak: Would you mind if I asked you a couple of questions about it?
quests.instruction: Repeat with the same smooth, connected delivery.

quests.hint: Blend 'what do you' and 'think we should'.
quests.explanation: Frustration or puzzlement often shows in fast, compressed function words. 'What do you' and 'think we should' shrink, so the real question, DO and WHOLE THING, is heard.
quests.textToSpeak: What do you think we should do about the whole thing?
quests.instruction: Match the speaker's connections between words.

quests.hint: Peaks on DIS-a-GREE and TIME; link 'think it through'.
quests.explanation: The sentence corrects a misunderstanding: you do not disagree, you need time. Stress on DIS-a-GREE and TIME shows the contrast, and linking 'think it through' keeps the thought moving.
quests.textToSpeak: It's not that I disagree; it's just that I'd like more time to think it through.
quests.instruction: Follow the speaker closely and copy every part of the delivery.

quests.hint: Beats on KNOWN, A-VOID-ed, PROB-lem; weak 'could have'.
quests.explanation: Formal conditional inversion sounds smooth when 'could have' shrinks to 'could-əv' and the content words carry the rhythm.
quests.textToSpeak: Had we known earlier, we could have avoided the whole problem.
quests.instruction: Repeat as naturally as the model, keeping the same shape.

quests.hint: Beats on CARE-ful-ly, PLAN, ALL-ways, WRONG.
quests.explanation: The two clauses mirror each other: how you plan, and what goes wrong. The pause after 'plan' lets the second clause answer the first.
quests.textToSpeak: No matter how carefully you plan, something always seems to go wrong.
quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then reproduce the phrase with the same feeling.

quests.hint: Link 'grab a quick word' and 'head out'.
quests.explanation: Asking for a quick conversation should sound light, so 'grab a' and 'head out' are compressed. QUICK WORD then carries the message that the request will be short.
quests.textToSpeak: Could I just grab a quick word with you before you head out?
quests.instruction: Repeat with the same smooth, connected delivery.

quests.hint: Link 'out of the office' and 'until Monday'.
quests.explanation: An out-of-office message is a routine statement, so it flows quickly. 'Out of the' shrinks so that OFF-ice and MON-day are heard.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll be out of the office until Monday, but I'll check my email.
quests.instruction: Match the speaker's connections between words.

quests.hint: Link 'send that over by the end of the day'.
quests.explanation: A polite deadline request sounds more natural when the long phrase 'by the end of the day' flows as one unit. 'Send that over' also links, so the request sounds relaxed.
quests.textToSpeak: If you could send that over by the end of the day, that'd be perfect.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then repeat as one smooth stream.

quests.hint: Keep 'strengths' crisp, with no extra vowel.
quests.explanation: 'Strengths' ends in three consonants, /ŋθs/. Keep them quick and precise, and let 'simplicity' and 'flexibility' carry their beats.
quests.textToSpeak: The strengths of the plan are its simplicity and its flexibility.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then repeat with crisp, complete sounds.

quests.hint: Say /ksθ/ in 'sixth'; link 'out of'.
quests.explanation: 'Sixth' ends in three consonants, so the tongue must move quickly to the teeth. 'Out of' links smoothly, which leaves the effort for the difficult sound.
quests.textToSpeak: We finished sixth out of forty teams.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and keep every sound as clear as theirs.

quests.hint: Keep /ldz/ in 'world's', /ndz/ in 'thousands'.
quests.explanation: Words like 'world's' and 'thousands' end in three consonants, and the last two are voiced. Keeping the voicing prevents them from turning into /s/, which would change the meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: The world's biggest firms spend thousands on staff development.
quests.instruction: Listen closely to the endings and sounds, then repeat.

quests.hint: Chunk: 'Right, so' / 'let me quickly recap where we are' / 'then open it up for questions'.
quests.explanation: Long introductions rely on chunks: pausing between the four groups keeps the sentence natural.
quests.textToSpeak: Right, so let me quickly recap where we are, then open it up for questions.
quests.instruction: Follow the speaker closely and copy every part of the delivery.

quests.hint: Peaks on GOOD, HON-est and KNOW.
quests.explanation: An honest 'I don't know' sounds confident when the pace is steady. Stress on GOOD, HON-est and KNOW shows appreciation, honesty and the actual answer in that order.
quests.textToSpeak: That's a really good question, and I think the honest answer is that we don't know yet.
quests.instruction: Repeat as naturally as the model, keeping the same shape.

quests.hint: Peak on FAIR and CON-trol.
quests.explanation: 'To be fair' is a softener before a defence, so it is quick. The peak on CON-trol then gives the reason the delays were not the team's fault.
quests.textToSpeak: To be fair, most of the delays came from factors outside our control.
quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then reproduce the phrase with the same feeling.

quests.hint: Keep the pace even; link 'feel the same way'.
quests.explanation: Empathy sounds sincere when it flows, so 'feel the same way' should be smooth. Stress on com-PLETE-ly, FRUS-trat-ed and po-SI-tion shows that you are taking the customer's side.
quests.textToSpeak: Look, I completely get why you're frustrated, and I'd feel the same way in your position.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker in real time, keeping pace.

quests.hint: Rise on 'refund', fall on 'prefer'.
quests.explanation: The rise on 'refund' marks the first option and the fall on 'prefer' closes the choice. 'We can' and 'if you'd' are weak because the options matter more than the grammar.
quests.textToSpeak: We can offer a full refund, or arrange a replacement if you'd prefer.
quests.instruction: Listen, then repeat at the same natural speed.

quests.hint: Link 'look into it' and 'get back to you'.
quests.explanation: A promise to follow up sounds reliable when it flows. 'Look into it' and 'get back to you' are stock phrases, so they run together as chunks.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll look into it straight away and get back to you by end of day.
quests.instruction: Shadow the whole line in one go, keeping up with the model.

quests.hint: Peaks on TECH-nol-o-gy and A-GREE; link 'getting everyone'.
quests.explanation: The sentence corrects a common assumption: the problem is people, not technology. TECH-nol-o-gy and a-GREE are the contrast, and 'getting everyone' links so it does not slow the second half.
quests.textToSpeak: Honestly, the biggest challenge isn't the technology; it's getting everyone to agree on how we use it.
quests.instruction: Repeat as naturally as the model, keeping the same shape.

quests.hint: Peaks on CON-straints and re-MARK-a-bly.
quests.explanation: The opening clause justifies the result, so it is said quickly. The peak on re-MARK-a-bly then lands on the positive verdict.
quests.textToSpeak: Given the constraints we're working with, I think we've done remarkably well.
quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then reproduce the phrase with the same feeling.

quests.hint: Peaks on HON-est, MAKE and PULLED to-GETH-er.
quests.explanation: A story with a turn: the pause after 'honest', a peak on MAKE, then a warm rise-fall on 'pulled together'.
quests.textToSpeak: If I'm being completely honest, I wasn't sure we'd make it, but the team really pulled together.
quests.instruction: Match the speaker's pacing, stress and pitch as you repeat.
